sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **The popular-searches list no longer offers words someone was still typing.** The list is read from the search log, and the log holds a row per distinct query text — which includes every prefix a shopper types on the way to a word. Those prefixes collect hits beside real queries and surface as suggestions: on a 12 500-product shop three of the ten suggestions on offer were "ipho", "iph" and a half-typed model. A row is now dropped when a more popular row starts with it and the next character there is a letter — a word cut mid-way. Anything else ends the word and the longer query is simply a different one: a space ("чехол" under "чехол iphone"), punctuation ("чехол" under "чехол-книжка"), and a digit, which is the case worth naming — model numbers grow by digits, so "a51" under "a515" is two real models of one line and hiding the shorter would hide a product the shop sells. Two limits come with it, both deliberate: a word form built by adding letters cannot be told from a truncation by shape alone, so a singular goes under a more popular plural; and a number abandoned mid-way stays. Both leave one extra suggestion, where the alternative loses a real one. Measured on that shop's log: nine of the hundred most searched phrases were half-written, none of the single-word queries behind them were touched. The search itself is not affected in any way, only what the empty search box offers, and it costs no extra query and no scheduled task: the list already reads the log behind an hourly cache, and the row that unmasks a half-written word is by definition more popular, so it is already in the same slice — 1.20 ms before against 1.34 ms now, once an hour.
